A car $C$ drives toward a $108\,\text{m}$ high building $B$ following a straight path. The angle of elevation $\theta $ made by the car and the top of the building $T$ is increasing at a rate of $\frac{\pi }{36}$ radians per second. What is the speed of the car when $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14212968/assets/f28ca3385d2179984c29d27a06926806e445c1dbab2cfa5f9fd6857149b632bb.png)

  

In the figure, $x$ is the distance between the car and the building, and $y$ is the building's height. The quantity $y=108$ meters does not change with time because the building's height is fixed.

We wish to calculate $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$
To do this, let's start by setting up a relation between $x$ and $y.$ Relative to the angle $\theta ,$ the sides $x$ and $y$ are the adjacent and opposite, respectively. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x}{y} \\ \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x}{108} \\ x & =108\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(108\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =(-108{csc}^{2}⁡\theta )\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given information, we have $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=\frac{\pi }{36}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Substituting these values into the above, we reach

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =(-108{csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}))\frac{\pi }{36} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-108{(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3})}^{2}\frac{\pi }{36} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-3\pi (\frac{4}{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =-4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the car is $4\pi \,\text{m/s}.$
